test_title: PYST 2: SSC CPO - English Comprehension (Held On 09 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: english
question:
A sentence is provided in indirect speech. From the four given options, choose the one that most accurately conveys the sentence in its corresponding direct speech.

The trainer remarked that participants must arrive 15 minutes early for registration.

options.text: “Participants had to come 15 minutes early for registration,” the trainer remarked.
“Arrive 15 minutes early for registration,” the trainer told the participants.
“you will be registered only if you arrive 15 minutes early,” said the trainer.
“It's mandatory to register before 15 minutes,” said the trainer.

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** The trainer remarked that participants must arrive 15 minutes early for registration.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **"must arrive" becomes the imperative "Arrive"**
 
 
• When a direct imperative command or strong instruction ("Arrive 15 minutes early") is reported, it is frequently converted using a "that" clause with a modal verb of obligation like "must" or "should." Reversing this gives us the direct imperative verb "Arrive."
 
 
 
• **Reporting verb and structure:**
 
 
• The phrase "the trainer told the participants" naturally sets up the direct command. When converted to indirect speech, this command is summarized as a remark about an obligation ("remarked that participants must...").
 
 
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:**
 
 
• The direct command is enclosed in quotation marks, begins with a capital letter, and is separated from the reporting clause by a comma.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Arrive 15 minutes early for registration," the trainer told the participants.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "Participants had to come 15 minutes early for registration," the trainer remarked.

 
 
• Changes the verb from "arrive" to "come" and uses the past obligation "had to," which does not represent the original command as accurately as an imperative.
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** "you will be registered only if you arrive 15 minutes early," said the trainer.
 
 
• Introduces a conditional clause ("only if") and changes the sentence structure entirely, altering the original meaning.
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** "It's mandatory to register before 15 minutes," said the trainer.
 
 
• Rephrases the sentence too loosely, adds unnecessary vocabulary ("mandatory"), and changes "15 minutes early" to "before 15 minutes," which changes the literal timeline.
